subject.title: Feature: Include trusted sender_name in inbound metadata envelope

question: Which sender identity fact should OpenClaw expose as trusted inbound metadata for agents: a raw platform display name, a stable provider ID, or a configured canonical principal such as session.identityLinks?
rationale: The current code deliberately excludes human-readable names from trusted system metadata; changing that boundary affects spoofing resistance, privacy, prompt-cache stability, and message routing correctness.

options.title: Use Configured Principal
options.body: Expose only a canonical principal resolved from stable provider IDs through an operator-owned mapping such as session.identityLinks, while leaving display names in untrusted context.

options.title: Expose Raw Display Name
options.body: Add a trusted sender display-name field from channel profile lookups, accepting the privacy and spoofing semantics as a product decision.

options.title: Defer To Chat Authorship Contract
options.body: Pause this issue until the broader chat.send per-message author/provenance model defines a shared identity contract across gateway and channel ingress.

recommendation.title: Use Configured Principal
recommendation.body: Expose only a canonical principal resolved from stable provider IDs through an operator-owned mapping such as session.identityLinks, while leaving display names in untrusted context.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the current trusted/untrusted metadata boundary is the sender-spoofing hardening commit in this area.
